newsitem.title: USA: National hopes for fame, innovation, with Cyrix.
newsitem.headline: National hopes for fame, innovation, with Cyrix.

text.p: National Semiconductor Corp. was one of a handful of companies that set roots in an arid San Francisco suburb 30 years ago and created what became Silicon Valley, the capital of the computer industry.

But while the other companies -- Fairchild Semiconductor, Zilog, Intel -- went on to claim fame for the invention of the microprocessor and revolutionising the way the world works, National remained a sleepy maker of commodity electronic components for personal computer equipment and cellular phones.
Now, Santa Clara, Calif.-based National hopes to make up for that by acquiring Cyrix Corp., a maker of low-cost microprocessors for cheap PCs, for $550 million.

Together, the companies hope to be the innovators in an emerging business that industry giant Intel Corp. so far has been slow to embrace: Cheap network computers and other so-called information appliances.
"With this acquisition, we have now put into place all the pieces and building blocks necessary to put a complete PC system on a chip," said Brian Halla, National's chief executive.

Reducing the functions of a PC onto a single chip would let PC makers make machines for about $500. At that price, the number of PC-like devices sold each year could jump to 700 million from 70 million now, Halla said.

Although Intel has said it plans to make parts for low-cost PCs, it has been reluctant to give up huge profits from its microprocessors and has been slow to move. Halla hopes to exploit this, analysts said.

Still, acquiring Cyrix is a huge gamble, analysts said. Cyrix has had little success gaining market share in the $20 billion microprocessor business against Intel and distant No. 2 player Advanced Micro Devices Inc., even though it sells its chips for much less.
"I believe in the vision Brian has of a system on a chip, but National seems to be paying a steep price," said Dan Niles, chip analyst at Robertson Stephens & Co.
National is in the second phase of a corporate restructuring that began more than two years ago under former Chairman Gilbert Amelio.
After posting losses of $151.4 million in the fiscal year ended in May 1991, National posted a profit of $27.5 million in the fiscal year that just ended in May.
National is positioning itself as a leader in semiconductors for analogue, linear or mixed-signal markets.
With Cyrix, it's also aiming for the cheap network PC, a market with a promising future but no firm idea how big it will really be.
Since Halla came to National in 1996, his priority has been to move the company into more profitable businesses, either by buying other companies or product lines.

In March, National bought Mediamatics Inc., a maker of chips that handle the sound and video capabilities of PCs. National also in March dumped its Fairchild Semiconductor unit, which makes logic and memory chips.
